verdict.root_cause: cartservice is not failing — it is waiting. Every sampled cart handler span is dominated by its Redis child span, with only ~1-3ms of handler self time, and every Redis operation sits on a near-identical ~300ms floor with almost no spread (tr_24bd427232c9). Total handler latency scales with operation count (one op ≈ 300ms for GetCart/EmptyCart, two ops ≈ 600ms for AddItem), which is the signature of a fixed per-operation stall on the cart datastore rather than load-driven queueing inside cartservice. That delay propagates upward unchanged into frontend CartService calls and checkoutservice PlaceOrder, which is why checkout, frontend and loadgenerator alerted within 15s of cartservice while cartservice's own error ratio stayed flat at zero across every sample point (tr_41f3f9fb809d, tr_88acdc24abc6) and its logs showed only normal INFO handler traces with widened inter-operation spacing (tr_65cb49d3ff3c). The failing mechanism is a slow dependency on the cart read/write path, absorbed as latency rather than errors.
verdict.reasoning: The trace decomposition is the load-bearing evidence: child Redis spans consume essentially the whole parent duration, which excludes cartservice's own code, GC or CPU saturation as the time sink (tr_24bd427232c9). Two independent metric queries confirm the error ratio is a defined zero at 59 and 61 sample points respectively, so the service was up, serving, and not rejecting anything — the failure is purely a wait, not a fault (tr_41f3f9fb809d, tr_88acdc24abc6). Logs corroborate the same shape from a different angle: continuous normal handler entries with no dependency error, no restart banner, but sharply degraded per-request spacing late in the window (tr_65cb49d3ff3c). The tight clustering of every Redis child near a common ~300ms floor, additive by operation count and insensitive to payload, argues for an imposed fixed delay on the datastore path rather than organic contention, which is why I name config_revert as the likely fix — but note the classification rule that a setting which inserts delay into a call path is still dependency_latency, because the wait is the mechanism, not a wrong address or credential. The change queries found nothing (tr_68d4b60528fd, tr_e350de7d65d2), and both explicitly flag that they covered only 05:31-05:46 rather than the full requested hour, so they do not exclude a change landing between 04:41 and 05:31; they only exclude one co-timed with onset. The retrieved cart-redis-misconfig incident matches the surface pattern — cart at flat-zero error rate misread as healthy while upstream services page — but it is a prior, not a finding here.
open_questions: No change history was ever queried for 04:41-05:31; the specific act that introduced the ~300ms per-operation delay is unidentified, so the remediation target is inferred from the latency signature rather than from a change record.

No specialist was dispatched to Redis / the cart datastore itself. Whether the ~300ms floor originates in the Redis instance, in a proxy or sidecar on the connection path, or in a client-side setting inside cartservice is unresolved — and that determines where the fix goes.

cartservice's p95/p99 latency, request rate, CPU/memory, throttling and connection-pool saturation were explicitly not returned (tr_88acdc24abc6), so a resource-pressure contribution at the cart or Redis client layer is unmeasured rather than excluded.

The log result was truncated and omitted the region containing 05:41:45 (tr_65cb49d3ff3c), so there is no direct observation of what cartservice logged at the moment of onset — the exact transition time is inferred, not seen.

Empty-userId GetCart calls appear only in the late log segment and are unexplained; they may be an unrelated client artifact or a symptom of upstream timeout/retry behaviour, and nothing here settles which.

Whether this is a fixed injected delay or a Redis instance that became uniformly slow (e.g. persistence, swap, or a network path change) is not distinguished by the traces alone; if it is the latter, config_revert is the wrong remediation.
